title: Chromatic polynomials of signed graphs with a balancing vertex

definitions.name: x2611_16458_balanced
definitions.lean:
def x2611_16458_balanced {V : Type*} (P N : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ ε : V → Bool,
    (∀ v w, P.Adj v w → ε v = ε w) ∧
    (∀ v w, N.Adj v w → ε v ≠ ε w)
definitions.notes: Balance is expressed by the equivalent switching characterization stated in Subsection 2.1: a Boolean sign at each vertex makes positive endpoints equal and negative endpoints different. Opposite signed parallel edges make this impossible, so unbalanced two-edge cycles are retained.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_zeroFree
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16458_zeroFree {V : Type*} [Finite V]
    (P N : SimpleGraph V) : Polynomial ℤ := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite V
  exact Finset.sum (P.edgeFinset.disjSum N.edgeFinset).powerset (fun F =>
    let P' : SimpleGraph V := SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {e | Sum.inl e ∈ F}
    let N' : SimpleGraph V := SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {e | Sum.inr e ∈ F}
    if x2611_16458_balanced P' N' then
      Polynomial.C ((-1 : ℤ) ^ F.card) *
        Polynomial.X ^ Nat.card (P' ⊔ N').ConnectedComponent
    else 0)
definitions.notes: The zero-free chromatic polynomial, defined by finite inclusion-exclusion over signed edge subsets. A balanced selected edge set contributes (-1)^|F| q^(number of components); an unbalanced component forces a forbidden zero color and contributes zero. Positive and negative copies of the same undirected edge are separately tagged. This is a construction of the paper’s coloring polynomial, not an assumption of any audited result. For N=bottom it is the ordinary chromatic polynomial P_G.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_numerator
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16458_numerator (n : ℕ) (p : Polynomial ℤ) : Polynomial ℤ :=
  Finset.sum (Finset.range (n + 2)) (fun i =>
    Polynomial.C (Finset.sum (Finset.range i) (fun j =>
      (-1 : ℤ) ^ j * ((n + 1).choose j : ℤ) *
        p.eval ((i - j - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))) * Polynomial.X ^ i)
definitions.notes: For a degree-n polynomial p=Z, these are the coefficients of (1-t)^(n+1) times the formal series sum_{q≥1} p(q-1)t^q from (1.2). Coefficient i is the binomial convolution over j<i; choosing n+1 over j is zero outside its natural range. Terms through degree n+1 are included, as in the paper. All statements instantiate p with the zero-free coloring polynomial on n vertices.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_isBlock
definitions.lean:
def x2611_16458_isBlock {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) : Prop :=
  (∃ v ∈ S, ∃ w ∈ S, G.Adj v w) ∧
  (G.induce S).Connected ∧
  (∀ v ∈ S, (G.induce (S \ {v})).Connected) ∧
  ∀ T : Set V, S ⊆ T →
    (∃ v ∈ T, ∃ w ∈ T, G.Adj v w) →
    (G.induce T).Connected →
    (∀ v ∈ T, (G.induce (T \ {v})).Connected) → T = S
definitions.notes: A block is represented by its vertex set: a maximal induced connected subgraph with at least one edge that stays connected after deleting any vertex. Blocks of a loopless graph with the paper’s possible opposite signed parallel edges are induced on their vertex sets, and parallel edges do not change cut vertices. Two-vertex bridges and opposite-sign digons are both included.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock
definitions.notes: Existence of a block whose inherited signs are balanced. Connectivity and cut vertices use the union P ⊔ N; inherited signs use both graphs separately.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_split
definitions.lean:
def x2611_16458_split {V : Type*} (P N : SimpleGraph V) (u : V) :
    SimpleGraph (Bool ⊕ {v : V // v ≠ u}) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun a b => match a, b with
    | Sum.inl s, Sum.inl t => s ≠ t
    | Sum.inl s, Sum.inr w => if s then P.Adj u w.val else N.Adj u w.val
    | Sum.inr v, Sum.inr w => P.Adj v.val w.val
    | _, _ => False)
definitions.notes: H_u(Σ) from Subsection 2.4: inl true is u_+, inl false is u_-, and inr vertices are the remaining original vertices. The two split vertices are joined. fromRel symmetrizes the displayed incidences and excludes loops. Each use assumes every negative edge is incident to u, so retaining only positive edges among remaining vertices is exactly the printed construction.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_twoConnected
definitions.notes: The paper’s definition: at least three vertices, connected, and connected after deleting any one vertex.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_beta
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16458_beta {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℤ :=
  (-1 : ℤ) ^ Nat.card V * (x2611_16458_zeroFree G ⊥).derivative.eval 1
definitions.notes: The graphic beta invariant (-1)^|V| P_G′(1), exactly as defined before (2.6). The ordinary polynomial P_G is the zero-free polynomial with all edges positive.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_blockBetaProduct
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16458_blockBetaProduct {V : Type*} [Finite V]
    (P N : SimpleGraph V) (u : V) : ℤ := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite V
  exact Finset.prod (Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Set V => x2611_16458_isBlock (P ⊔ N) S))
    (fun S => if hu : u ∈ S then
      x2611_16458_beta (x2611_16458_split (P.induce S) (N.induce S) ⟨u, hu⟩)
    else 1)
definitions.notes: The block product b_Σ in Proposition 3.1. Under its hypotheses every block is unbalanced, contains a negative edge, and therefore contains u. The else branch makes the definition total outside those hypotheses and is never used for the audited proposition.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_edges
definitions.lean:
def x2611_16458_edges (n : ℕ) (E : List (ℕ × ℕ)) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun v w => (v.val + 1, w.val + 1) ∈ E)
definitions.notes: Concrete simple graph specified by a list of undirected edges using the paper’s labels 1,...,n. fromRel supplies the reverse orientations and excludes loops.

definitions.name: x2611_16458_blockPolynomialProduct
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16458_blockPolynomialProduct {V : Type*} [Finite V]
    (P N : SimpleGraph V) : Polynomial ℤ := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite V
  exact Finset.prod (Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Set V => x2611_16458_isBlock (P ⊔ N) S))
    (fun S => x2611_16458_zeroFree (P.induce S) (N.induce S))
definitions.notes: Product of Z_B over all blocks, represented by their vertex sets with inherited signs. The empty product is one. This only packages the product in (2.2); no factorization assertion is built into the definition.

statements.label: Theorem 1.1
statements.name: x2611_16458_thm1_1
statements.original:
Let $\Sigma$ be a connected loopless signed graph on $n\geq 2$ vertices with a balancing vertex.
Then the following conditions are equivalent:

(i) 

There exists an ordinary graph $G$ such that

 $\chi_{\Sigma}(q)=\chi_{G}(q),\qquad\text{equivalently,}\quad Z_{\Sigma}(q)=P_{G}(q).$ 

(ii) 

Every coefficient of $h_{\Sigma}(t)$ is nonnegative.

(iii) 

 $\Sigma$ has a balanced block.

(iv) 

 $Z_{\Sigma}(1)=0$ , equivalently, $\chi_{\Sigma}(2)=0$ .

Moreover, whenever these conditions hold, the graph $G$ can be chosen to be connected, simple, and to have $|V|$ vertices.

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_bal
    {V W : Type*} (e : V ≃ W) (P N : SimpleGraph W) :
    x2611_16458_balanced (P.comap e) (N.comap e) ↔
      x2611_16458_balanced P N := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hp, hn⟩
    refine ⟨fun w => f (e.symm w), ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v w h
      exact hp _ _ (by simpa using h)
    · intro v w h
      exact hn _ _ (by simpa using h)
  · rintro ⟨f, hp, hn⟩
    exact ⟨fun v => f (e v), fun _ _ h => hp _ _ h, fun _ _ h => hn _ _ h⟩

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indconn
    {V W : Type*} (e : V ≃ W) (G : SimpleGraph W) (S : Set W) :
    ((G.comap e).induce (e ⁻¹' S)).Connected ↔ (G.induce S).Connected := by
  let f : (e ⁻¹' S) ≃ S :=
    { toFun := fun v => ⟨e v, v.property⟩
      invFun := fun w => ⟨e.symm w, by simpa using w.property⟩
      left_inv := fun v => by ext; simp
      right_inv := fun w => by ext; simp }
  exact (show (G.comap e).induce (e ⁻¹' S) ≃g G.induce S from
    { f with map_rel_iff' := by intros; rfl }).connected_iff

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indbal

    x2611_16458_balanced ((P.comap e).induce (e ⁻¹' S))
      ((N.comap e).induce (e ⁻¹' S)) ↔
      x2611_16458_balanced (P.induce S) (N.induce S) := by
  let f : (e ⁻¹' S) ≃ S :=
    { toFun := fun v => ⟨e v, v.property⟩
      invFun := fun w => ⟨e.symm w, by simpa using w.property⟩
      left_inv := fun v => by ext; simp
      right_inv := fun w => by ext; simp }
  exact x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_bal f (P.induce S) (N.induce S)

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_poly
    {V W : Type*} [Finite V] [Finite W] (e : V ≃ W) (P N : SimpleGraph W) :
    x2611_16458_zeroFree (P.comap e) (N.comap e) = x2611_16458_zeroFree P N := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite V
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite W
  let s : Sym2 V ≃ Sym2 W :=
    { toFun := Sym2.map e
      invFun := Sym2.map e.symm
      left_inv := by intro z; induction z using Sym2.inductionOn; simp
      right_inv := by intro z; induction z using Sym2.inductionOn; simp }
  let d := Equiv.sumCongr s s
  have hedges : ((P.comap e).edgeFinset.disjSum (N.comap e).edgeFinset).map
      d.toEmbedding = P.edgeFinset.disjSum N.edgeFinset := by
    ext z
    obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := d.surjective z
    simp only [Finset.mem_map_equiv, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
    cases z with
    | inl z => induction z using Sym2.inductionOn; simp [d, s]
    | inr z => induction z using Sym2.inductionOn; simp [d, s]
  have hleft (F : Finset (Sym2 V ⊕ Sym2 V)) :
      (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inl z ∈ F.map d.toEmbedding}).comap e =
        SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inl z ∈ F} := by
    ext v w
    simp [SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj, Finset.mem_map_equiv, d, s, e.injective.ne_iff]
  have hright (F : Finset (Sym2 V ⊕ Sym2 V)) :
      (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inr z ∈ F.map d.toEmbedding}).comap e =
        SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inr z ∈ F} := by
    ext v w
    simp [SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj, Finset.mem_map_equiv, d, s, e.injective.ne_iff]
  unfold x2611_16458_zeroFree
  apply Finset.sum_equiv d.finsetCongr
  · intro F
    simp only [Finset.mem_powerset, Equiv.finsetCongr_apply, ← hedges,
      Finset.map_subset_map]
    rfl
  · intro F hF
    simp only [Equiv.finsetCongr_apply, Finset.card_map]
    let Q : SimpleGraph W := SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inl z ∈ F.map d.toEmbedding}
    let R : SimpleGraph W := SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inr z ∈ F.map d.toEmbedding}
    have hb := x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_bal e Q R
    rw [hleft, hright] at hb
    rw [hb]
    split_ifs with h
    · have hc : Nat.card (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inl z ∈ F} ⊔
          SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inr z ∈ F}).ConnectedComponent =
          Nat.card (Q ⊔ R).ConnectedComponent := by
        have hh : (Q ⊔ R).comap e =
            SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inl z ∈ F} ⊔
              SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {z | Sum.inr z ∈ F} := by
          change Q.comap e ⊔ R.comap e = _
          rw [hleft, hright]
        rw [← hh]
        exact Nat.card_congr (SimpleGraph.Iso.comap e (Q ⊔ R)).connectedComponentEquiv
      rw [hc]
    · rfl

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_edge
    {V W : Type*} (e : V ≃ W) (G : SimpleGraph W) (S : Set W) :
    (∃ v ∈ e ⁻¹' S, ∃ w ∈ e ⁻¹' S, (G.comap e).Adj v w) ↔
      (∃ v ∈ S, ∃ w ∈ S, G.Adj v w) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, w, hw, h⟩
    exact ⟨e v, hv, e w, hw, h⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, w, hw, h⟩
    exact ⟨e.symm v, by simpa using hv, e.symm w, by simpa using hw, by simpa using h⟩

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_del
    {V W : Type*} (e : V ≃ W) (G : SimpleGraph W) (S : Set W) :
    (∀ v ∈ e ⁻¹' S, ((G.comap e).induce ((e ⁻¹' S) \ {v})).Connected) ↔
      (∀ w ∈ S, (G.induce (S \ {w})).Connected) := by
  have heq (v : V) : e ⁻¹' (S \ {e v}) = (e ⁻¹' S) \ {v} := by
    ext x
    simp [e.injective.eq_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h w hw
    have hh := (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indconn e G (S \ {e (e.symm w)})).mp
      (by rw [heq]; exact h (e.symm w) (by simpa using hw))
    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hh
    exact hh
  · intro h v hv
    rw [← heq]
    exact (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indconn e G (S \ {e v})).mpr (h _ hv)

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_block
    {V W : Type*} (e : V ≃ W) (G : SimpleGraph W) (S : Set W) :
    x2611_16458_isBlock (G.comap e) (e ⁻¹' S) ↔ x2611_16458_isBlock G S := by
  unfold x2611_16458_isBlock
  apply and_congr (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_edge e G S)
  apply and_congr (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indconn e G S)
  apply and_congr (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_del e G S)
  constructor
  · intro h T hs he hc hd
    apply (Set.preimage_injective.mpr e.surjective)
    exact h (e ⁻¹' T) (Set.preimage_mono hs)
      ((x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_edge e G T).mpr he)
      ((x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indconn e G T).mpr hc)
      ((x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_del e G T).mpr hd)
  · intro h T hs he hc hd
    let U : Set W := e.symm ⁻¹' T
    have hTU : e ⁻¹' U = T := by ext; simp [U]
    have hsU : S ⊆ U := by
      intro w hw
      exact hs (by simpa using hw)
    have heU := (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_edge e G U).mp (by rwa [hTU])
    have hcU := (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indconn e G U).mp (by rwa [hTU])
    have hdU := (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_del e G U).mp (by rwa [hTU])
    have hh := congrArg (fun A : Set W => e ⁻¹' A) (h U hsU heU hcU hdU)
    simpa only [hTU] using hh

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_hasblock
    {V W : Type*} (e : V ≃ W) (P N : SimpleGraph W) :
    x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock (P.comap e) (N.comap e) ↔
      x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock P N := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨T, hb, hbal⟩
    let S : Set W := e.symm ⁻¹' T
    have hTS : e ⁻¹' S = T := by ext; simp [S]
    refine ⟨S, ?_, ?_⟩
    · apply (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_block e (P ⊔ N) S).mp
      change x2611_16458_isBlock (P.comap e ⊔ N.comap e) (e ⁻¹' S)
      rwa [hTS]
    · apply (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indbal e P N S).mp
      rwa [hTS]
  · rintro ⟨S, hb, hbal⟩
    exact ⟨e ⁻¹' S, (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_block e (P ⊔ N) S).mpr hb,
      (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indbal e P N S).mpr hbal⟩

theorem x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv : (∀ (n : ℕ) (P N : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (hconn : (P ⊔ N).Connected)
    (hbal : ∃ u : Fin n, x2611_16458_balanced
      (P.induce {v : Fin n | v ≠ u}) (N.induce {v : Fin n | v ≠ u})), ((∃ m : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin m), x2611_16458_zeroFree P N = x2611_16458_zeroFree G ⊥) ↔ (∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ (x2611_16458_numerator n (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N)).coeff i)) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ (x2611_16458_numerator n (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N)).coeff i) ↔ x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock P N) ∧
    (x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock P N ↔ (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N).eval 1 = 0) ∧
    ((x2611_16458_zeroFree P N).eval 1 = 0 ↔ ((x2611_16458_zeroFree P N).comp (Polynomial.X - 1)).eval 2 = 0) ∧
    ((∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ (x2611_16458_numerator n (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N)).coeff i) → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.Connected ∧
      x2611_16458_zeroFree G ⊥ = x2611_16458_zeroFree P N)) ↔ (∀ {V : Type*} [Finite V] (P N : SimpleGraph V) (hn : 2 ≤ Nat.card V) (hconn : (P ⊔ N).Connected) (hbal : ∃ u : V, x2611_16458_balanced (P.induce {v | v ≠ u}) (N.induce {v | v ≠ u})), ((∃ m : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin m), x2611_16458_zeroFree P N = x2611_16458_zeroFree G ⊥) ↔ (∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ (x2611_16458_numerator (Nat.card V) (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N)).coeff i)) ∧ ((∀ i : ℕ, 0 ≤ (x2611_16458_numerator (Nat.card V) (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N)).coeff i) ↔ x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock P N) ∧ (x2611_16458_hasBalancedBlock P N ↔ (x2611_16458_zeroFree P N).eval 1 = 0) ∧ ((∃ m : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin m), x2611_16458_zeroFree P N = x2611_16458_zeroFree G ⊥) → ∃ G : SimpleGraph V, G.Connected ∧ x2611_16458_zeroFree P N = x2611_16458_zeroFree G ⊥)) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro hA V _ P N hn hconn hbal
    let e : Fin (Nat.card V) ≃ V := (Finite.equivFin V).symm
    let P' := P.comap e
    let N' := N.comap e
    have hc : (P' ⊔ N').Connected :=
      (SimpleGraph.Iso.comap e (P ⊔ N)).connected_iff.mpr hconn
    have hb : ∃ u : Fin (Nat.card V), x2611_16458_balanced
        (P'.induce {v | v ≠ u}) (N'.induce {v | v ≠ u}) := by
      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hbal
      refine ⟨e.symm u, ?_⟩
      have hs : e ⁻¹' {v : V | v ≠ u} = {v | v ≠ e.symm u} := by
        ext v
        simp [Equiv.eq_symm_apply]
      have ht := (x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_indbal e P N {v | v ≠ u}).mpr hu
      rw [hs] at ht
      exact ht
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, h5⟩ := hA (Nat.card V) P' N' hn hc hb
    have hp := x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_poly e P N
    have hh := x2611_16458_thm1_1_eqv_aux_hasblock e P N
    simp only [P', N', hp, hh] at h1 h2 h3 h5
    refine ⟨h1, h2, h3, ?_⟩

statements.original:
The following statements hold.

(a) 

Suppose that signed graphs $\Sigma_{1}$ and $\Sigma_{2}$ have exactly one common vertex and no common edges.
Then $\displaystyle Z_{\Sigma_{1}\cup\Sigma_{2}}(q)=\frac{Z_{\Sigma_{1}}(q)Z_{\Sigma_{2}}(q)}{q}$ .
Consequently, if a connected signed graph $\Sigma$ has blocks $B_{1},\ldots,B_{b}$ , then

(2.2)

 $Z_{\Sigma}(q)=q^{1-b}\prod_{i=1}^{b}Z_{B_{i}}(q).$ 

(b) 

Suppose that ordinary graphs $G_{1}$ and $G_{2}$ meet exactly in an edge and its two endpoints. Then

(2.3)

 $P_{G_{1}\cup G_{2}}(q)=\frac{P_{G_{1}}(q)P_{G_{2}}(q)}{q(q-1)}.$

statements.original:
Let $\Sigma$ be the graph consisting of an unbalanced $C_{3}$ with one negative edge and two isolated vertices.
Then

 $Z_{\Sigma}(q)=q^{3}(q^{2}-3q+3),\qquad\chi_{\Sigma}(q)=(q-1)^{3}(q^{2}-5q+7),$ 

and

 $h_{\Sigma}(t)=t^{2}+2t^{3}+48t^{4}+62t^{5}+7t^{6}$ 

has nonnegative coefficients.
On the other hand, $Z_{\Sigma}(1)=1$ . Any ordinary graph with an edge has $P_{G}(1)=0$ , while an edgeless graph on five vertices has polynomial $q^{5}$ , different from $Z_{\Sigma}(q)$ .
Therefore, no ordinary graph has chromatic polynomial $Z_{\Sigma}(q)$ .
This shows that connectedness cannot be omitted even if only the equivalence between (i) and (ii) is retained.
